Hi Oleg,

Reminder: this offering is closing.

At the launch of its new GPT-6 “Astra” model this month, OpenAI president Greg Brockman made a bold declaration: the “AGI era” has begun.¹

In plain terms, AGI refers to AI that can match or surpass humans across virtually every cognitive task. OpenAI’s own bar is systems that “outperform humans at most economically valuable work.”¹, ²

OpenAI calls Astra its “most intelligent and aligned” model yet. In one demo, it finished a job search in under three minutes that OpenAI said would take a person roughly five hours.²

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang put it plainly: “AGI has arrived.”¹

To be clear, there’s no agreed-upon definition of AGI, and researchers caution that no single benchmark proves we’ve crossed the line.¹, ²

But step back from the semantics, and one thing is clear: amid fierce competition with Anthropic and other rivals, OpenAI is still one of the leading names pushing AI forward.

There’s no guarantee that OpenAI’s technology, revenue, or valuation will continue to grow, or that the company will be profitable. See the risk disclosures on the offering page.

79550.subject: The Price Is the Product
79550.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Crypto’s reflexivity never ceases to amaze me. Price rises, the protocol captures attention, new users try the product, and fundamentals improve, reinforcing the narrative that attracted everyone in the first place. Derive is the latest example.

Last week, a few prominent voices on X[ argued](https://x.com/tulipking/status/2100051477033071048?s=20) that Derive remained undervalued, while traders shared screenshots of OTM positions[ executed](https://x.com/koolkrypto223/status/2099141525850747001?s=20) on the platform. The resulting attention helped drive a more than 170% rally in DRV last week and drew more traders to the product, contributing to an all-time high of $1.26B in weekly options volume. Through Sep. 20, monthly options volume had already reached $2.37B, 24% above the previous record with ten days still remaining.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2756fb5a-e325-442f-983e-6ae22bc00358/image.png?t=1790043602)
Caption: 

To assess whether higher volume was accompanied by broader participation, we looked at daily active traders and the number of options trades. Derive averaged 459 daily traders last week, up 68% week over week and the highest full-week average since February 2025. Options trade count increased 83% to nearly 11,800.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fc75679e-d381-4cd7-bdec-dda62b4845a1/image.png?t=1790043603)
Caption: 

ETH reclaimed its position as Derive’s largest options market after an extended period of BTC-led activity, generating $632M in weekly volume versus $520M for BTC. Activity also continued to expand beyond the two majors, with HYPE contributing $58M and ZEC reaching $37M, nearly four times its prior week’s volume. ZEC traded throughout all seven days, while both trade count and average trade size increased sharply.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/30e4412d-cc0d-4541-afb5-2266a0faa4a6/image.png?t=1790043601)
Caption: 

The increase in activity was accompanied by greater demand for upside convexity. ETH traders bought roughly $95M of outright OTM calls measured by underlying notional, including sizable exposure to $4,000-$5,000 strikes for 2027, although some of the largest prints formed part of structured call spreads. ZEC offered an even clearer example of speculative positioning, with traders buying calls struck as much as 145% above spot. The flow was not purely short-dated speculation, but it clearly included traders reaching for cheap, far-OTM calls offering highly asymmetric payoffs.
